question.text: A convex lens of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> forms an image of an extended source of light on a photoelectric cell. A current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>I</mi></math> is produced. The lens is replaced by another convex lens having the same diameter but focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math>. The photoelectric current now is

solution.text:
For a light of any given frequency, the photoelectric current is directly proportional to the intensity of light.

As the diameter of the lens remains the same, both lenses will collect the same amount of light. Therefore, the intensity of the light will remain the same.

Hence, this is the correct option.
